- **Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA)**
  - Systemic inflammatory vasculitis affecting large and medium vessels
  - Most commonly affects temporal arteries
  - Can lead to irreversible vision loss if untreated
  - Urgent treatment required with high-dose corticosteroids

- **Epidemiology**
  - Age: Almost exclusively >50 years old, peak 70-80 years
  - Gender: Female > Male (3:1 ratio)
  - Race: More common in Caucasians, especially Scandinavian descent
  - Associated with polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) in 40-50% of cases

- **Clinical presentation**
  - Headache: New onset, temporal, persistent
  - Jaw claudication: Pain with chewing (highly specific)
  - Visual symptoms: Transient vision loss (amaurosis fugax), diplopia, permanent vision loss
  - Scalp tenderness: Pain when combing hair or sleeping
  - Constitutional symptoms: Fever, weight loss, fatigue
  - PMR symptoms: Proximal muscle pain and stiffness

- **Diagnostic workup**
  - ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate): Usually >50 mm/hr, often >100 mm/hr
  - CRP (C-Reactive Protein): Elevated
  - Temporal artery biopsy: Gold standard, shows granulomatous inflammation with giant cells
  - Skip lesions possible, so negative biopsy doesn't exclude diagnosis
  - Consider bilateral biopsy if high clinical suspicion
  - Don't delay treatment waiting for biopsy

- **Treatment**
  - Immediate high-dose corticosteroids: Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day (40-60 mg/day)
  - If vision loss present: IV methylprednisolone 1g/day for 3 days
  - Start treatment immediately if clinical suspicion high
  - Don't wait for biopsy results
  - Long-term taper over 12-18 months guided by symptoms and inflammatory markers

- **Complications**
  - Vision loss: Most serious, can be irreversible
  - AION (Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy): Most common cause of vision loss
  - CRAO (Central Retinal Artery Occlusion)
  - Diplopia from cranial nerve palsy
  - Stroke: Rare but serious

- **Follow-up**
  - Monitor ESR/CRP during taper
  - Watch for steroid side effects: Hyperglycemia, hypertension, osteoporosis, infections
  - Consider bone protection: Calcium, vitamin D, bisphosphonates
  - Taper slowly based on clinical response
  - Relapse common during taper
